cards.title: Introduce remarketing only after audience lists reach a workable threshold
cards.claim: Remarketing campaigns can have significant effects when set up correctly, but the passage recommends introducing them later in the account when conversions and data are coming in and there is a steady stream of new customers; if customer lists are too small, targeting is too restricted to run them.
cards.action: Before launching remarketing, ensure audience lists and data segments are in place; wait until customer lists reach a certain threshold before running these campaigns.
applies_when: account has conversions coming in, data coming in, and a steady stream of new customers arriving
audience lists have started populating with customers
setting up remarketing for an e-commerce account later in its lifecycle
do_not_use_when: account is only just set up and audience lists are not populated
targeting would be too restricted because the list is too small
unknowns: the exact numeric threshold for audience list size
how to determine the 'certain point in the account'
how long it takes for lists to populate sufficiently
evidence_quotes: this is a more minor campaign type into in comparison to the previous campaigns that we've been discussing, but it can still have some very significant effects on your account when set up correctly and can produce some really great results.

I would certainly recommend introducing these campaign types when you reach a certain point in the account. uh when you have conversions coming in, data coming in, and you have a steady stream of new customers arriving, you can start to remarket to those customers, increase your conversion rates, increase your acquisition, and get more profit coming into the account.
Before setting up anything remarketing wise, we need to make sure that we have our audience lists and data segments in check.
If your customer lists are too small, um it's just not going to allow you to to target people because it's it's too targeted.
so, you have to wait until you get to a certain threshold before you can start running these.
I recommend introducing them later on the account. Not only because it's best practice, but also because it's necessary to introduce them later on.

cards.title: Display remarketing: sales objective, purchases, low initial budget, conversion-value bidding
cards.claim: For display remarketing in e-commerce, the passage recommends sales objective and purchases conversion goal; a fairly low budget because high display budgets can push low-quality placements; conversion value focus/maximize conversion value bidding; and delaying target ROAS until data is gathered, or setting a low target if enabled early.
cards.action: Create a display campaign with sales objective and purchases conversion goal; start around $10 a day or $15 a day and scale slowly; use conversion value focus/maximize conversion value bidding; delay target ROAS until data is gathered, or set a really low target if enabled from the beginning.
applies_when: setting up a display remarketing campaign
account is at a point where conversion-based bidding can be used
acquiring data and testing whether remarketing is effective
do_not_use_when: no conversion data for conversion-based bidding
considering enabling target ROAS from the get-go without a low target
using a high budget that may push low-quality display placements
unknowns: the exact cap for scaling budget
how much data is needed before using target ROAS
what counts as a 'really low' target return on ad spend
evidence_quotes: Once again, campaign objective is sales.
Conversion goals, purchases, always, always purchases.
Campaign type, display today.
for remarketing, we can work with a fairly low budget.
you don't want to be going too high unless until you're seeing, you know, positive results within scalability
if you give a really high budget to display, it will just push out really low quality placements.
starting out around $10 a day, you know, $15 a day, whatever it may be
So I'd usually go with conversion value focus and that will allow us to maximize our conversion value.
also target return ad spend this is something that could be useful to implement after you've gathered a bit of data in the campaign.
I wouldn't recommend or uh enabling it from the get- go.
if you do enable it from the beginning, make sure to set a really low target return on ad spend so you can actually get some prospecting out there and um you won't restrict the campaign.

cards.title: Use automatic Google Ads tag and G4/J4 audiences for most remarketing; optional Shopify customer-match import
cards.claim: The passage recommends direct automatic setup with Google Ads tag and G4/J4 as the easiest and most reliable way to get audience data for the vast majority, unless more complex targeting is needed; it also notes linking Shopify and GA4/J4, and says a Shopify customer match list plugin can quickly import customers but is not necessary.
cards.action: Set up Google Ads tag and G4/J4 for automatic audience lists; link Shopify and G4/J4 to Google Ads; optionally use a Shopify customer match list plugin to import existing customers; in campaign targeting, add audience segments.
applies_when: setting up remarketing audience lists for most e-commerce stores
need to feed more data into the account
